Andersen-Patterson Clinic

Dear Colleague,

I saw Jocelyn Rodriguez in consultation on August 06, 2025. Ms. Rodriguez presented with concerns related to her abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) and heart failure/cardiomyopathy. I appreciate the detailed referral and the opportunity to collaborate on her care.

**Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm (AAA):**
Ms. Rodriguez's AAA, measuring 4.3 cm, was successfully repaired 40 months Currently, the aneurysm remains controlled, and no additional medications are required. During her last visit, her blood pressure was 117/69 mmHg, and her weight was 118 pounds, both within normal limits. 

**Heart Failure / Cardiomyopathy:**
Ms. Rodriguez's heart failure and cardiomyopathy, with an ejection fraction (EF) of 53%, have been effectively managed. Her condition has remained stable and controlled for approximately 9.3 years. There are no current indications for additional medications.

**Examination:**
On physical examination, Ms. Rodriguez had normal vital signs and no significant abnormalities were noted. Her cardiovascular and respiratory exams were within normal limits. 

**Social History:**
Ms. Rodriguez exercises regularly, running 3-4 times per week, which excellent for her cardiovascular health. She has a history of tobacco use, having smoked 10 cigarettes per day since 2008, but she quit in March 2024. She also consumes alcohol at a rate of approximately 12 drinks per week.

**Impression and Recommendations:**
Ms. Rodriguez’s abdominal aortic aneurysm and heart failure/cardiomyopathy remain well-controlled with current management strategies. Regular follow-up
